thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 latency alert for /v1/generate in prod — current p99 = 3.2s (SLO 2.0s). Detected at 2026-03-14T02:12:03Z. Tags: kv-cache, stream, model=redwood-13b

Ashwin (oncall): seeing it too. p95 jumped to ~600ms, p99 3.2s. streaming stalls increased. starting triage.

Priya (oncall): assigning. @Miguel can you pull KV cache metrics (eviction rate, fragmentation, prefill hit/miss)?

Miguel (infra): grabbing metrics — one sec.

Miguel (infra): metrics snapshot: kv_eviction_rate ~= 420/s, kv_prefill_miss_rate 0.68, kv_cache_fragmentation = 42%, kv_cache_size_bytes ~ 820GB (shard target 64GB).

Liam (runtime): that eviction rate is huge. smells like prefill > decode imbalance — large prefill traffic filling distinct prefixes so cache shards thrash.

Ashwin (oncall): any correlate with traffic pattern? new customer deploy? Jenna, any CS reports?

Jenna (cust-ops): Customer Ops got 5 tickets about slow streaming responses starting ~02:05Z. Major account A reported repeated stalls for long generations.

Priya (oncall): ok, impact = production customers seeing streaming stalls and higher tail latency. Need mitigation path: 1) reduce prefill aggressiveness, 2) increase soft limit for cache eviction cooldown, 3) fallback route to smaller model for heavy tail. Thoughts?

Liam (runtime): quick win: toggle prefill off for redwood-13b on prod pool via admin feature-flag. That will reduce writes to kv cache and should reduce eviction pressure. downside: cold decodes may be slower initially but tail should drop.

Miguel (infra): I can flip feature flag. Which flag? kv_cache.prefill_enabled for pool=prod-13b?

Priya (oncall): yes. Also prepare to scale up shards if flipping causes other regressions.

Ashwin (oncall): before we change, snapshot p95/p99 and active streams count.

Miguel (infra): saving dashboards and grabbing traces. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc/latency?from=now-15m

Priya (oncall): ok Miguel, flip flag now and watch tail. Ping when done.

Miguel (infra): running: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/flags -d '{"flag":"kv_cache.prefill_enabled","value":false,"selector":"pool:prod-13b"}'

deploy-bot: deploy started for feature flag kv_cache.prefill_enabled -> false (id: ff-84723)

Miguel (infra): done. deploy-bot shows success.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for ff-84723 across prod-13b pool (70 nodes).

Liam (runtime): I'm seeing p99 drop from 3.2s to 1.9s in the first 90s on the sampled shard set. streaming stalls count down from 120/min to 18/min.

Ashwin (oncall): nice. p95 also down to 420ms. eviction rate fell to ~95/s. fragmentation slowly decreasing.

Jenna (cust-ops): Customer Ops: telling affected customers we applied mitigation and ask for confirm.

Priya (oncall): good. Next steps: 1) keep flag off for 2 hours to let cache re-balance, 2) schedule a controlled cache shard resize for non-peak, 3) investigate root cause — why prefill load spiked (recent rollout? big prompt patterns?).

Liam (runtime): I'm looking at recent model config rollout — there was a change to prefill_size_limit on redwood-13b two hours ago from 32->128 tokens in canary -> prod. That explains increased prefill pressure.

Miguel (infra): noted. I'll revert the config param in canary and open a rollback if we see reoccurrence.

Ashwin (oncall): action items: MIGUEL revert prefill_size_limit change in config; LIAM run offline sim of workload distribution vs kv shard mapping; PRIYA keep monitoring and prepare fallback route to redwood-7b-q4 if tail creep resumes. Jenna send short customer update.

Miguel (infra): Created PR to revert prefill_size_limit: https://git.redwood/infra/kv-config/pull/512

Priya (oncall): monitoring window 02:15Z -> 04:15Z. if p99 > 2.0s for more than 10m we'll re-escalate and open incident page.

Ashwin (oncall): handoff: I'm going off-call at 04:00Z. Priya please take next-pager for this incident. Full context in this thread. :white_check_mark:

Priya (oncall): taking handoff. If anything regresses, ping @pager immediately. I'll also run eviction tuning script (increase cache_eviction_cooldown to 4s) if fragmentation doesn't drop below 30% in 30m.

Jenna (cust-ops): emailed affected customers with mitigation and ETA for follow-up: "We've applied a temporary mitigation that reduces prefill to stabilize latency; our engineering team is investigating a recent config change that increased prefill limits. We'll follow up with a root cause update."

Liam (runtime): note for postmortem: correlate prefill metric spikes with commit history and with per-customer prompt length distributions. Also add synthetic runner to detect prefill-induced thrash earlier.

Ashwin (oncall): any objections to closing this Slack thread as 'mitigated' after 2 hours of stable metrics?

Priya (oncall): fine by me. I'll escalate if anything pops.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: p99 returned below SLO threshold. Auto-close window in 2h unless reopened.

Miguel (infra): I'll keep the rollback PR as high priority; will merge once tests pass.

Priya (oncall): thanks team. I'll file a short incident record and link traces + PRs to it.

Ashwin (oncall): good job everyone.

Jenna (cust-ops): closing loop with customers once postmortem ready. :thumbsup:
